title: Rights Readback V1 (what GET /api/projects/<id>/rights answers)
$comment: Written against three payloads the product really emitted on 2026-10-22 -- a project holding one APPROVED scope plus one DENIED scope, a project whose only scope is APPROVED, and a project nobody filed anything for -- captured through design_lab.http_service.make_server on a live socket; see design-lab/scripts/verify_route_payload_contracts.py. Emitter: src/design_lab/rights_review.py (readback). THE DECISIONS ARE REFERENCED, NOT RESTATED: every element of `decisions` and every value of `current_decisions` is the rights decision itself, bound by design-lab/schemas/contracts/rights-decision.schema.json. Copying those fields here would create a second authority able to disagree with the contract the write path already enforces, so a v1 decision change moves into this file by reference. `rights_clearance` is the one word a reader can be misled by, and the rule behind it is bound below rather than left to prose: CLEARED requires at least one filed scope and cannot be carried by an empty set, so 0-of-0 reads NOT_REVIEWED. PENDING_REVIEW never appears here as a clearance -- it is a word a human may file inside `decision_states`, never one this facade infers.

decision_states.$comment: One entry per word the decision contract allows, including zero -- a vocabulary member that silently disappeared from this map is how a state word stops being emittable without anything going red.

ever_filed_scopes.$comment: Scopes with any row, including ones retired by supersede. Kept apart from `current_decisions` so a retired decision cannot be read as no decision ever having existed.

scope_conflicts.$comment: A forked chain: more than one live row for one scope. The facade picks the newest for `current_decisions` and publishes the fork here instead of hiding the tie-break.

name_checked_only.$comment: Scopes whose current decision states no actor kind. Over this boundary no decision can carry one, so HTTP-filed rows land here; an empty list would mean a declared kind, which the contract cannot express.

allOf.$comment: The clearance rule, machine-checked: CLEARED is a sentence about the project, so it may not be carried by an empty scope set nor by part of one. filed_scope_count and approved_scope_count travel with the word precisely so a reader never has to trust the word alone.

The same rule read from the other side: 0-of-0 is vacuously 'all approved' and must never be reported as cleared. An emitter that starts computing clearance with `all(...)` over an empty scope set violates this document, not just the prose above it.
